summary: This is the main SKILL.md of Refero's agent skill, a research-first methodology for AI agents doing UI and product design. It says every design must be grounded in references before implementation, using three research layers: styles for visual direction, screens for concrete UI patterns, and flows for multi-step journeys. It teaches agents to pick one dominant reference and preserve its sharp traits rather than averaging several references into a safe middle, and to keep each token in the role its source gave it. Before building, the agent writes a design brief, a reference lock and a decision ledger that traces every major choice to a reference, a user constraint or a craft rule. It ends with craft rules aimed at avoiding generic AI design defaults and a quality gate checklist, which matters to a design system builder because it shows how to keep a chosen direction from drifting into the bland centroid.
key_ideas: Research references before any design work instead of relying on the model's generic taste.
Use three research layers: styles for look and feel, screens for concrete UI patterns, flows for journeys.
Do not copy one reference and do not average several; choose one dominant direction and borrow 1-2 narrow details.
Keep token roles from the source: a CTA color stays CTA-only, syntax colors stay inside code, decorative gradients stay decorative.
Write a short brief first and ask only for information that would materially change the result.
Lock the direction before building with a reference lock: primary source, traits to preserve, borrowed details, role rules, media strategy, rejects, token commitments.
Convert research into a decision ledger; a major choice with no source is researched more, tied to a constraint, or removed.
Choose the lightest workflow: direct build, visual exploration with three options, audit, or asset generation.
Match research depth to task risk.
Preserve imagery roles; an honest, well-sized placeholder beats a weak fake illustration made of CSS.
Treat calm editorial looks, cream canvases, earthy palettes, decorative headline word swaps and default indigo/violet as AI-slop risks unless research justifies them.
Create at least one memorable detail users would remember.
Validate the rendered build against the locked target and fix drift before handoff.

claims.claim: Generic frontend or product design skills tend to pull work back toward generic AI design.
claims.evidence: Non-Negotiables: generic design skills tend to pull work back toward generic AI design

claims.claim: Refero styles currently cover web marketing and product pages, not in-app dashboards, auth screens, settings screens or iOS app screens.
claims.evidence: Current limitation: Refero styles currently cover web marketing/product pages

claims.claim: A style is a semantic design reference extracted from a real web page, not a screenshot and not a component library.
claims.evidence: Use Styles First For Visual Work

claims.claim: Averaging conflicting references produces a bland result, e.g. dark, acid and serif references collapse into warm cream, muted orange and a polite serif.
claims.evidence: Synthesis rule: the answer is not warm cream + muted orange + polite serif

claims.claim: Image generation can be slow and may not exist in every coding environment.
claims.evidence: Non-Negotiables: Use image generation only when it changes the outcome

claims.claim: Calm editorial styling is a current AI-slop risk.
claims.evidence: Core craft rules: Treat "calm editorial" as a current AI-slop risk

claims.claim: Pricing pages commonly put the billing toggle above plan cards, highlight one plan and move detailed feature comparison below.
Cancellation flows usually collect a reason, offer an alternative, confirm the destructive action and state when access ends.

quotes: Do not average references into a safe middle.
A brief is not a build target.

rules.rule: Ground every design in researched references before implementation instead of the model's generic design taste.
rules.why: The source says not to rely on the model's generic design taste; references give taste and product evidence.
rules.evidence: Non-Negotiables: Research before design work

rules.rule: When references conflict, choose one dominant direction, preserve its sharp traits and let secondary references add only narrow details.
rules.why: Averaging collapses the direction into a safe middle.
rules.evidence: Do not average references into a safe middle

rules.rule: Do not copy a single reference; study several strong references and synthesize a new direction for the product.
rules.why: The result should be a new direction inspired by several references, not a copy.
rules.evidence: Do not copy one reference

rules.rule: Use a token only for the role its source assigns: CTA colors stay CTA-only, syntax colors stay inside code, decorative gradients stay decorative.
rules.why: Repurposing tokens changes their meaning and breaks the direction.
rules.evidence: Do not change token meanings; Never move a token outside its source role

rules.rule: Do not turn a CTA accent into a background, a code-only color into UI chrome, or a decorative gradient into an interface surface.
rules.why: Token roles from references must be preserved.
rules.evidence: Core craft rules: Preserve token roles from references

rules.rule: Keep card and button rules at their specified radius, shadow and state behavior when borrowing them.
rules.why: The source says never to move a token outside its source role, and lists card and button rules among those roles.
rules.evidence: card/button rules keep their specified radius, shadow, and state behavior

rules.rule: If the primary style is image-led, keep the image slot with stable dimensions, aspect ratio, caption or alt text and an art-direction note rather than switching to a text-only layout.
rules.why: The media role is part of the style; weak fakes are worse than an honest placeholder.
rules.evidence: If the primary style is image-led, do not replace it with text-only layout

rules.rule: Do not fake complex imagery with weak CSS, text or decorative boxes.
rules.why: An honest, well-sized placeholder beats a poor fake illustration or photo.
rules.evidence: Respect imagery guidance

rules.rule: Write a reference lock (primary direction, 3-5 traits to preserve, 1-2 borrowed details, role rules, media strategy, rejects, token commitments) before implementation.
rules.why: It stops implementation drifting into safer colors, fonts, radius or generic layouts.
rules.evidence: Before implementation, create a reference lock

rules.rule: If implementation drifts from the lock, stop and correct it; do not soften distinctive traits into safer colors, fonts, softer radius or generic section layouts.
rules.why: Softening loses the chosen direction.
rules.evidence: If implementation drifts from the lock, stop and correct it

rules.rule: Before implementation, fill a decision ledger with Decision, Source, Source rule / role and Why for each major choice, and remove any major choice that has no source.
rules.why: Every major choice must trace to a reference, user constraint or craft rule.
rules.evidence: convert research into a short decision ledger

rules.rule: In discovery, ask only for missing information that would materially change the result; otherwise assume and proceed.
rules.why: Keeps the brief short without blocking work.
rules.evidence: Discovery

rules.rule: For variants, a new visual language, a major redesign or a landing page, default to three reference-locked options and ask the user to choose.
rules.why: High-visibility surfaces have several plausible directions.
rules.evidence: Workflow Routing: Visual exploration

rules.rule: Use image generation only for visual exploration, mockups, imagery, illustrations, textures and difficult assets; skip it for small fixes, obvious production edits or code-native UI.
rules.why: It can be slow and may not exist in every environment.
rules.evidence: Use image generation only when it changes the outcome

rules.rule: Use styles, not screens, as the primary source for visual direction; use screens afterwards for structure and concrete details.
rules.why: Styles are the layer for visual direction and taste; screens are for structure and concrete UI patterns.
rules.evidence: Avoid using screens as the primary style source when the task is visual

rules.rule: Define tokens before implementation: type scale, colors, spacing, radius, shadows.
rules.why: Core craft rule after research.
rules.evidence: Core craft rules

rules.rule: Do not default to indigo or violet unless the user explicitly asks for it; use brand-appropriate colors from research.
rules.why: Listed as a generic AI design default.
rules.evidence: Core craft rules: Do not default to indigo/violet

rules.rule: Do not default to decorative headline word swaps (one word or short phrase set in a different display, serif, script or italic style or accent color) unless research and product context justify them.
rules.why: The source treats calm editorial as a current AI-slop risk, and the quality gate checks for these swaps.
rules.evidence: Treat "calm editorial" as a current AI-slop risk

rules.rule: Do not default to warm ivory or cream canvases or olive, clay or terracotta palettes unless research and product context justify them.
rules.why: The source lists these as part of the calm editorial look it treats as a current AI-slop risk.
rules.evidence: Core craft rules: Treat "calm editorial" as a current AI-slop risk

rules.rule: Avoid the generic hero, features grid, pricing, FAQ, CTA page sequence unless research supports it.
rules.why: It is a generic AI design default.
rules.evidence: Avoid generic hero -> features grid -> pricing -> FAQ -> CTA

rules.rule: Use text-wrap: balance on headings and short display text, use text-wrap: pretty selectively for prose, and check key breakpoints for orphan words.
rules.why: Avoids orphan words and awkward final lines.
rules.evidence: Core craft rules: Balance headings

rules.rule: Create at least one memorable detail: a visual move, interaction, layout choice or copy detail.
rules.why: Users should remember something about the design.
rules.evidence: Create at least one memorable detail

rules.rule: Use real product evidence for copy, trust signals, objection handling and section order.
rules.why: Avoids invented content decisions.
rules.evidence: Core craft rules

rules.rule: Build accessibility and responsive behavior into the design, not as a late pass.
rules.why: Core craft rule.
rules.evidence: Keep accessibility and responsive behavior in the design

rules.rule: After building visual work, compare the rendered implementation against the locked target and fix actionable drift before handoff.
rules.why: Research alone is not sufficient.
rules.evidence: Validate after building visual work

rules.rule: Give the user a short research summary before designing a non-trivial task instead of dumping every result.
rules.why: Keeps findings readable.
rules.evidence: Present Findings

rules.rule: Make research output specific: name the references, describe concrete choices and explain what will be adapted.
rules.why: Stated as a non-negotiable so that every decision can be traced.
rules.evidence: Non-Negotiables: Research output must be specific

rules.rule: Before implementation, lock a build target: a user-provided visual source, an existing product or design-system target, a selected generated mockup, or an approved reference-locked direction; a brief alone is not enough.
rules.why: A brief is not a build target.
rules.evidence: Non-Negotiables: A brief is not a build target

rules.rule: When combining styles, give each source a bounded job, for example one owns canvas and type, another the code-window treatment, another the primary CTA.
rules.why: Keeps borrowed details from spreading beyond their role.
rules.evidence: When combining styles, assign each source a bounded job

rules.rule: Build simple diagrams, icons, code windows or geometric primitives only when they match the source style.
rules.why: Code-native stand-ins must fit the primary style's media role.
rules.evidence: Build simple diagrams, icons, code windows, or geometric primitives only when they match the source style

rules.rule: Preserve the primary reference's strongest traits instead of normalizing them.
rules.why: Normalizing traits collapses the chosen direction.
rules.evidence: Core craft rules

rules.rule: Present the result as a new direction inspired by several references, never as copying one.
rules.why: The aim is a new direction for the user's product, not a clone.
rules.evidence: Never present the result as "copying X"

rules.rule: Before final delivery, run the quality gate checklist; if any answer is no, research or refine more before delivering.
rules.why: Catches copying, averaging, lost token roles and generic AI defaults before handoff.
rules.evidence: Quality Gate

rules.rule: Load bundled craft references only when relevant; do not load every file by default.
rules.why: Stated in the Design Craft section [inferred: keeps context small].
rules.evidence: Design Craft: do not load every file by default

decisions.question: Which workflow fits this design task?

options.name: Direct build
options.effect: Research and lock the direction, then code straight away.
options.when: Small UI fixes, clear production edits, existing design-system work, or a concrete source to match.

options.name: Visual exploration
options.effect: Three reference-locked options the user chooses between.
options.when: Variants, a new visual language, a major redesign, a landing page or another high-visibility surface.

options.name: Audit
options.effect: Critique grounded in screenshots, screens or flows as evidence.

options.name: Asset generation
options.when: The reference lock needs bitmap media that code, icons or existing assets cannot provide.

decisions.recommendation: Choose the lightest workflow that can produce a high-quality result.

decisions.question: How do you combine several references that point in different directions?

options.name: Copy one reference
options.effect: A clone of someone else's product.

options.name: Average all references
options.effect: A safe, bland centroid such as warm cream, muted orange and a polite serif.

options.name: One primary plus borrowed details
options.effect: The primary style sets mood, density and structure; secondary styles add 1-2 bounded details.

decisions.recommendation: One primary foundation with 1-2 borrowed details, each source given a bounded job, because averaging loses the sharp traits.
decisions.evidence: Synthesis rule; Do not average references into a safe middle

decisions.question: Which research layer should answer this question?

options.name: Styles
options.effect: Look and feel: typography, palette, layout, spacing, radius, elevation, imagery.
options.when: Any task with a visual component; start here.

options.name: Screens
options.effect: What a screen contains: layout, hierarchy, components, CTAs, copy, states.
options.when: A specific screen type, component or UI pattern.

options.name: Flows
options.effect: Steps, decision points, confirmations, recovery and system responses.
options.when: Onboarding, signup, checkout, cancellation or any multi-step process.

decisions.recommendation: Combine layers: styles for visual direction, screens for patterns, flows for sequencing.

decisions.question: What do you put in an image slot when you cannot make the image the style needs?

options.name: Fake it in CSS or text
options.effect: Weak decorative boxes standing in for imagery.

options.name: Switch to a text-only layout
options.effect: Loses the image-led character of the style.
options.when: Never for an image-led primary style.

options.name: Intentional placeholder
options.effect: Stable dimensions, aspect ratio, caption or alt text and an art-direction note.
options.when: When real, generated or stock assets are not available.

decisions.recommendation: Use real, generated or stock assets when available; otherwise an honest, well-sized placeholder.
decisions.evidence: Respect imagery guidance; If the primary style is image-led

process.detail: Designing [WHAT] for [WHO] on [PLATFORM], with goal, tone, main objection, must-remember hook, constraints, research needed and path.
Pick direct build, visual exploration, audit or asset generation; the lightest that gives a high-quality result.
Search 3-5 visual angles (one broad aesthetic, one domain, one known brand), retrieve 3-4 full styles, compare, pick one primary and borrow 1-2 details.
Search by page type, component, state, company or on-screen text; extract layout, hierarchy, components, CTAs, copy, states and tactics.
For multi-step tasks, extract entry and exit, step count, decisions, friction reducers, confirmations, recovery, errors and system responses; broaden or reconstruct from screens if sparse.
Quick improvement: 2-3 style searches, 2-3 full styles, 1 short synthesis. New landing page or redesign: 3-5 searches, 3-4 full styles, plus screen research.
Visual direction from styles, product pattern from screens, journey logic from flows.
Primary direction, traits to preserve, borrowed details, role rules, media strategy, rejects and token commitments.
Give a short research summary and a decision ledger with source, role and reason for each choice.
Define tokens first, preserve roles and signature traits, avoid listed AI defaults.
Run the checklist and compare the rendered result to the lock; research or refine more if any answer is no.

examples.what: Visual direction synthesis for an analytics SaaS
examples.visual_note: White canvas, compact UI copy, restrained black primary actions, thin borders, product screenshots in framed panels, accent color kept rare.
Billing toggle above plan cards, one plan highlighted, detailed feature comparison moved below; hero kept quieter for a product that sells trust.
Collect a reason, offer a relevant alternative, confirm the destructive action, state when access ends, give a clear return path.
Queries like 'Linear changelog dark developer tool' and 'shadcn monochrome design system' show how to search by brand, domain and aesthetic.
Dark, acid and serif references averaged into warm cream, muted orange and a polite serif: the bland centroid to avoid.

caveats: This is a vendor's own skill: it insists on Refero MCP research and tells agents not to use generic design skills as a parallel design authority, which is self-promotion.
The style library is limited to web marketing and product pages, per the source's own stated limitation.
The AI-slop list (calm editorial, cream canvases, indigo/violet) is the authors' opinion of current trends and may date.
Linked reference files (typography.md, color.md, visual-workflow.md and others) were not part of this raw source.
